question: Which of the following Indian classical dance forms is known to be 'ekaharya'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatnatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bharatnatyam** is a major Indian classical dance form that originated in the **Tamil Nadu** region.
 
• The term **'ekaharya'** in Bharatnatyam refers to the **solo performance** of multiple roles by a single dancer.
 
• Bharatnatyam is characterized by **expressive hand gestures (mudras), intricate footwork, and facial expressions**.
 
• The dance form is deeply rooted in **spiritual themes** and is often performed as an offering to deities in temples.
 
• Bharatnatyam involves a combination of **Nritya (expressive dance) and Nritta (pure dance)** elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Abhinaya**: Refers to the art of expression in Indian classical dance, involving facial expressions, hand gestures, and body movements.
 
• **Natya Shastra**: An ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts written by Bharata Muni, which serves as the foundational text for Bharatnatyam.
 
• **Arangetram**: The debut performance of a Bharatanatyam dancer, marking their transition from student to professional performer.
 
• **Varnam**: A central piece in a Bharatnatyam repertoire, typically showcasing the dancer's technical prowess and expressive abilities.
 
• **Adavus**: Basic units of movement in Bharatnatyam, combining footwork, hand gestures, and body movements.
